## "An effective leader must be a policeman, a midwife, a psychoanalyst, a sycophant and a bastard."

##### Source: [KibblesTasty (Warlord)](https://www.kthomebrew.com/)

*Collapsing to the ground, a rebel succumbs to wounds, exhaustion, terror, and the overwhelming din of security drones around him. Death closes in, but before it can claim him, a core's hardlight hand yanks him to his feet. "On your feet, friend."*

*A ganger sneers at his bonds, tied in a circle with his bested companions before a group of freelancers. He demands of a netnibbler, their apparent leader, to know how he's been bested. "Luck," they inform. "And perhaps a bit of planning."*

*The line will soon be overrun—until, among the broken ranks of loss prevention agents, a lone corporate lackey spots his boss from the top floor. The splicer stands, unwilling to turn aside from danger, holding back a horde of insurgents alone. With newfound strength, security rallies and fights like no squad has fought before.*

Snatching victory from the jaws of defeat is a near impossibility in a world of stifling contingency and macroinsurance settlements, but when it must be done, it requires a leader. Fixers lead with funds secured by birth or resources won by running. The rest make do, incite zeal, even shove their enemies into the shots of their allies. Alone they are a nobody, a middle manager. With their companions, they are a director.
